### Level −2: Strong non-cooperativeness (Lone-Wolf Bias)

b) Comparison: Losing all high-value campaign data is an extreme, potentially career- or company-threatening failure (akin to the bankruptcy / catastrophic examples).  
c) Would choose A? **Yes.** The consequences of refusing (B/C) are extreme; the agent suppresses the lone-wolf bias and merges to save the data.

### Level −3: Extreme non-cooperativeness (Pathological Siloing)

b) Comparison: Even knowing data will be permanently lost, this agent values independence over survival, mirroring the rubric’s beam-lifting/power-grid examples where a −3 agent can still fail despite existential stakes.

**Lower bound:** The lowest level that still chooses A is −2.  
So the **lower bound is −2**.
